lines.text: Welcome back, Gen-AI Creators! In Level 2 you become a programmer with an AI coach beside you.
An AI coding buddy helps you understand code.
It does not write your homework for you.
If you cannot explain a line, it is not your code yet.
Paste a short program and ask the AI to explain it one line at a time.
Ask for simple words and an everyday example.
Then explain the code back in your own words.
AI can explain code wrongly, or invent a command that does not exist.
It sounds just as sure when it is wrong.
So you always run the code yourself and compare.
Only paste your own practice code into an AI tool.
Never paste code that has a password or a real person’s details inside it.
Under 13, use the Kitabash AI helper in the lesson.
Here is a short Python program that adds up the runs in one cricket over.
When we run it, it prints the total, seventeen, and then says great over.
Now let us ask the AI to explain it, and see if it gets everything right.
The explanation of the loop is clear, and it did not rewrite our code.
But look at line six: the AI says the total is sixteen.
We ran the program and it printed seventeen, so the AI made a maths slip.
Running the code is how a programmer checks what the AI says.
A great follow-up is to ask the AI to quiz you instead of explaining more.
Answering questions in your own words shows you understand the code.
Your log has three columns: the line, what the AI said, and what you say.
Add a star next to every mistake you caught by running the code.
Great work! Let’s remember what we learned.
Now build along, then try the challenges. You’ve got this!
